title: Compact-variant catalog GTM accelerator & release-note orchestration
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Ship a compact/quantized variant of an existing catalog model with a repeatable GTM accelerator checklist that covers benchmarks, console listing, SDK compatibility, documentation, release notes, and cross-team comms. This ticket coordinates the final validation gating and the release-note copy + announcement assets. Emphasis on: clear perf trade-offs, recommended defaults per deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private), and minimal customer disruption via canary rollouts and opt-in toggles.
checklist_items: Benchmarks: run standardized latency/throughput sweeps (seq len 32/128/512) and quality repros on core eval sets; capture 50th/95th/99th latency and tokens/sec; upload results to perf-dashboard and attach CSV

Quality regression matrix: run prompt set A/B (sanity + targeted safety prompts) and compare output metrics (perplexity where applicable, answer overlap, hallucination checks); flag cohorts with >5% drop in key metric
Quantization profile: document quantization settings tested (bits, kernels), expected memory & throughput gains, and known fidelity regressions; decide whether to enable by default for hosted API
Serving compatibility: validate model variant on hosted runtime, dedicated pools, and private deployment (VPC); note any kernel or compiler constraints and update runtime-compatibility table

Console listing: prepare catalog metadata (name, tags, family, recommended use-cases, max sequence length, pricing hint), thumbnail, short-summary (1–2 lines) and full description (why choose compact variant)
SDK/Client tests: run end-to-end SDK smoke tests (generation, chat, embeddings if applicable), bump compatibility matrix in SDK changelog
Release notes draft: prepare structured release note sections—Summary, Compatibility, Performance, Known Issues, Migration Path, Example Calls, FAQ—and circulate for review
Compliance & security: run checklist with Security (KMS implications for Private), Privacy review for telemetry, and include any redaction considerations in docs
Support playbook: create support-runbook with triage steps, known regressions, rollback instructions, and an automated query saved in observability dashboard
Rollout plan: define canary groups, traffic % ramps, SLO/alert thresholds (latency, error rate, quality regression signal), and rollback triggers
Announcement assets: draft blog blurb, short-form social copy, internal TL;DR, sales one-pager and sample customer emails
Release gating: require signoffs from Eng (perf + runtime), Docs, Security, and PM before enabling wide traffic; record approvals in this ticket
acceptance_criteria: Perf dashboard contains uploaded benchmark runs for seq len 32/128/512 with 50/95/99 latency and throughput exports
Quality regression checks executed and any failing cohorts documented with mitigation notes
Catalog entry created in Console with metadata and thumbnail, visible in staging catalog
Release notes draft approved by Docs and Eng and staged in release-notes repo
Rollout plan executed in smoke canary and metrics tracked; no critical regressions after 72h at 25% traffic
Support playbook and automated observability queries exist and are linked in ticket
Legal/Security signoff present if private deployment impacts sensitive telemetry

notes: Key trade-offs: prioritize throughput and cost for Dedicated customers while preserving answer quality for Hosted. Shipping plan uses opt-in quant for Hosted to give customers explicit control; default behavior for Dedicated will be aggressive quantization with clear telemetry. Keep rollout conservative for Private due to environment heterogeneity. Follow-up: schedule retrospective 2 weeks after wide launch to capture incidents and update the GTM accelerator checklist.
